regime.answer: September CPI printed hotter m/m and canonical TIPS/real‑yield evidence shows elevated real yields; nominal 10Y remains ~5.12% while ACM term premium eased, and credit breadth is mixed (HY widening but IG and large‑cap breadth still intact). This implies tightening driven by rates/real yields, not yet broad market stress.
regime.implication: Rates and real yields are tightening policy conditions; credit and breadth show pockets of stress but lack canonical evidence of broad contagion, so macro tightening is dominant for now.

stories.title: Mid‑October CPI and TIPS point to real yields accounting for much of the 10Y move
stories.whatChanged: BLS September CPI release plus canonical TIPS real‑yield observation for 14 Oct show higher real yields alongside nominal 10Y at ~5.12%.
stories.whyItMatters: If real yields explain most nominal movement, policy tightening is the dominant channel and long‑end persistence depends less on term premium or auction stress.
stories.mechanism: Higher realized inflation and real‑rate repricing lift real yields; a lower modelled term premium partially offsets nominal pressure, leaving real yields as the primary nominal driver.
stories.conclusion: Current canonical evidence supports a decomposition where elevated real yields are a major driver of nominal 10Y; ACM term‑premium evidence moderates the nominal impact but intraday persistence is unresolved.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Intraday Fed‑funds‑futures and 2Y/10Y 5m–30m bars showing no sustained front‑end repricing would weaken the real‑yield‑dominant interpretation.

stories.title: High‑yield spreads have widened materially while IG has been contained over the 20‑session window
stories.whatChanged: Diagnostics show pronounced HY OAS widening over 20 sessions with IG little changed, indicating concentrated credit pressure.
stories.whyItMatters: Selective HY stress could become broader if yields persist, testing credit resilience and funding conditions.
stories.mechanism: Issuer/sector‑specific risk or liquidity repricing can widen HY independently of IG; persistent yield elevation would risk spillover to IG and volatility.
stories.conclusion: Evidence supports concentrated HY widening with IG and breadth not yet confirming broad credit stress; the issue is watch‑list material for widening persistence.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical daily HY/IG series plus MOVE showing coordinated spread widening and rising volatility would confirm broad credit transmission.

stories.title: AI/semiconductor leadership is narrow: semis lag QQQ while large‑cap breadth stays elevated
stories.whatChanged: SMH underperformed QQQ over the 20‑session window while large‑cap breadth remained above long averages, signalling concentrated leadership within large caps.
stories.whyItMatters: Narrow leadership can sustain indexes despite tightening yields, delaying broad risk‑off if earnings and cash flows hold.
stories.mechanism: Earnings or concentration effects keep large caps afloat even as semiconductors and some AI names correct; durable resilience requires issuer cash‑flow and capex confirmation.
stories.conclusion: AI/semiconductor leadership is selective and does not yet imply a broad risk‑on; monitor issuer earnings, capex and credit to test durability.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Issuer filings showing widespread downgrades to AI/infra revenue or confirmed GPU order cancellations would overturn the ‘narrow resilience’ view.

investigations.question: Did the mid‑October CPI release materially reprice short‑end policy expectations and persist into later sessions?
investigations.whyItMatters: Persistence would shift the policy path and raise real‑rate and borrowing‑cost risks to growth and credit.
investigations.currentExplanation: Canonical CPI and elevated TIPS/real yields are present but intraday Fed‑funds‑futures and MOVE are missing, so immediate‑window persistence is unresolved.
investigations.expectedReaction: Conventional: hotter CPI would lift short‑end Fed‑funds repricing and push nominal yields higher.
competingExplanations: Initial front‑end repricing persisted vs initial spike faded as auction/term‑premium sequencing rebalanced yields.

candidateExplanations.explanation: Front‑end repriced on CPI and persisted while long end was offset by term‑premium moves.

candidateExplanations.explanation: Initial short‑end spike faded as auction/flow sequencing and ACM term‑premium moves dominated nominal direction.
candidateExplanations.discriminatingTest: Front‑end rates revert to pre‑print within 24–48 hours while ACM and auction metrics remain stable.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.
